Every TWS position update raises `AttributeError: 'Position' object has no attribute 'id'` at ui/active_portfolio_panel.py:308 (`strategy_by_id.get(pos.id, "—")`), reached via ui/main_window.py:3317 `self.portfolio_panel.add_position(position)` -> active_portfolio_panel.py:216 add_position -> :293 _group_and_render -> :308 _render_table. ROOT CAUSE: TWO unrelated dataclasses both named `Position`. The panel is written against data.models.Position (imported at active_portfolio_panel.py:23), which declares `id: Optional[int] = None` (data/models.py:89). But the live caller builds the object with ibkr.account.build_position_from_ib (ui/main_window.py:3293 -> ibkr/account.py:47), which returns ibkr.account.Position (ibkr/account.py:20-39) — a class with NO `id` attribute. ui/main_window.py:81 imports data.models.Position, so the annotation at :3337 (`position: Position`) and the panel's parameter annotation (active_portfolio_panel.py:210) both CLAIM data.models.Position while the runtime object is ibkr.account.Position. My own offscreen repro confirms: `hasattr(build_position_from_ib(...), 'id') is False`; `ActivePortfolioPanel().add_position(ibkr.account.Position)` raises the exact error; `set_positions([data.models.Position(...)])` does NOT raise (id defaults None). `.id` is also dereferenced at active_portfolio_panel.py:287/289 (option-leg grouping) and :222/:344/:364 (SL/TP, close). User-visible impact: the render aborts inside _render_table on EVERY update, so the Strategy/Group columns and per-row P&L never appear and AC-D27.6 ('the portfolio panel populates') is unmet. It is NOT a process crash in the shipped app: main.py:3 imports pyqtgraph before QApplication, and pyqtgraph/Qt/__init__.py:314-318 installs a non-abort `sys.excepthook`, so the traceback is printed on every update and the app keeps running (verified: real-path emit exits 0 and logs the traceback; a bare non-pyqtgraph app aborts). The bulk path ui/main_window.py:3319 _on_position_end does NOT crash (it builds data.models.Position) but is DEGRADED: its SELECT (:3323-3327) omits `id`, so every bulk-loaded position has id=None -> Strategy/Group render '—' and the SL/TP dialog early-returns (active_portfolio_panel.py:344 `if pos.id is None: return`), and _on_portfolio_sltp_changed persists via `WHERE id=?` (ui/main_window.py:3400).
expected: One position object on the wire: whatever is handed to ActivePortfolioPanel.add_position (and _upsert_position) carries a POPULATED `id` (the `positions.id` DB row key, db.py:86), so _render_table/_group_and_render can key strategy grouping and the SL/TP dialog + `UPDATE positions ... WHERE id=?` persistence work. Both the live update path (main_window.py:3281) and the _on_position_end bulk load (:3319) must supply it.

Concretely: make ibkr.account.Position carry `id` (or make it a subclass/alias of data.models.Position plus the `market_price` field the panel reads at active_portfolio_panel.py:386), and POPULATE it from the DB — have _upsert_position return the rowid (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(symbol,con_id) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING id`, or a follow-up SELECT) and set position.id, and add `id` to the _on_position_end SELECT (ui/main_window.py:3323). If converging on a single canonical model is judged an architecture decision rather than a code fix, route to Plan. Regression test (I write none): drive the real chain — emit ib_client.bridge.position_update with a stock contract and assert no exception and positions_table.rowCount()==1 with populated cells; and seed the DB then call _on_position_end and assert the row's id is non-None. An assertion on _positions membership alone is INSUFFICIENT (it passes while the render throws — see review_log coverage note).

observed: Fresh live-run defect report (repo main @ 29067af, clean tree). Clicking the toolbar 'Load Chart' button loads no chart and raises `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'strip'` at ui/main_window.py:1717 (`symbol = symbol.strip().upper()`). CAUSE: ui/main_window.py:223 `self.load_btn.clicked.connect(self.load_chart)`. Qt's QPushButton.clicked signal emits `clicked(bool checked=false)`; because commit 692bb61 (D28.2, 2026-10-13) parameterised the method as `load_chart(self, symbol=None, timeframe=None, extended_hours=None)` (main_window.py:1711), PyQt binds the emitted `False` to `symbol`, so symbol is not None and the else-branch :1716-1717 runs `False.strip()`. Verified offscreen: a QPushButton.clicked delivers `(False,)` to a slot that accepts args, and MainWindow.load_chart's first parameter is `symbol`; a 0-arg slot receives no args. REGRESSION: pre-D28.2 the method was `def load_chart(self):` (zero params), so PyQt dropped the bool entirely and the button worked; the `.strip()` on a caller-supplied symbol only exists from D28.2 onward. All other load_chart call sites are safe: :1337 `load_chart(symbol)` (str), :214 returnPressed (no-arg signal -> symbol=None -> widget path), :2952/:2971 `load_chart()` (no args). No other signal emitting a bool is wired to load_chart. Impact: the primary 'Load Chart' control is dead (and under PyQt's own default hook would abort; in the shipped app the pyqtgraph-installed excepthook swallows it, so one traceback is logged and nothing loads). The Enter-in-symbol-field and watchlist double-click paths still work, which is why the app is usable.
expected: Clicking 'Load Chart' with a symbol in the field loads that chart (equivalently `load_chart()` with symbol=None reading symbol_input), rather than raising. The D28.2 parameterised contract (AC-D28.2, requirements.md:2909/2932) must remain intact for the callers that pass explicit values (pop-outs, alarm monitor, tests).
suggested_direction: Decouple the bool-emitting signal from the parameterised method: `self.load_btn.clicked.connect(lambda: self.load_chart())` (or `functools.partial(self.load_chart)`), or coerce in the else-branch (`if isinstance(symbol, str): ... else: read the widget`). The lambda/partial is preferable — it keeps load_chart's signature exactly as D28.2 specifies. Note the same class of latent bug applies to any `clicked(bool)` / `toggled(bool)` / `triggered(bool)` signal wired to a slot whose first positional parameter is a value (e.g. if any other `*.connect(self.load_chart)`-style wiring is added later). Regression test (I write none): drive the toolbar path — set `win.symbol_input.setText('AAPL')`, call `win.load_btn.click()`, assert the chart was loaded for AAPL (or at minimum no exception). No current test does this: the suite calls `load_chart()`/`load_chart(sym, tf)` directly (e.g. tests/test_d28_2_sessions.py:145, tests/test_d24_smoke_gate.py:50) and never exercises the button's signal connection.

observed: Third runtime error from the same live TWS session (repo main @ 29067af, clean tree, 1028-test offscreen suite green; ESC-032/ESC-033 still open). Repeated three times: `RuntimeError: wrapped C/C++ object of type QTableWidgetItem has been deleted` at ui/watchlist_panel.py:992, inside the lambda `timer.timeout.connect(lambda: item.setBackground(QBrush(QColor('#101218'))))`. ROOT CAUSE — stale capture of a deleted C++ item across a table rebuild. ui/watchlist_panel.py:981-994 `_flash(row, key, color)` resolves the CURRENT cell item (:983 `item = self._item(row, key)`), highlights it (:986), creates a single-shot QTimer parented to the PANEL (:990 `timer = QTimer(self)`) and captures that item BY CLOSURE in the timeout lambda (:992), then start(400) (:993). `_rebuild_table` (ui/watchlist_panel.py:674-690, reached only via `_apply_columns` :692-696) replaces EVERY cell with a fresh QTableWidgetItem via `self.table.setItem(row, col, item)` (:690); Qt deletes the previous item at each (row,col). `_rebuild_table`/`_apply_columns` do NOT touch `_flash_timers`, so an in-flight 400 ms timer keeps its (row,key) entry (ui/watchlist_panel.py:994) and its closure reference to the now-deleted item, and fires 400 ms later against the freed C++ object. Because the timer is parented to `self` (the panel), it OUTLIVES the item that its callback closes over. My own offscreen repro (real WatchlistPanel, fake md manager) reproduces the exact traceback: `_flash(0,'last',GREEN)` -> `_apply_columns()` -> event loop past 400 ms -> RuntimeError at :992. `_apply_columns` is reachable ONLY from the watchlist header menu handlers — `_on_field_toggled` (:731-742, add/remove a column) and `_move_field` (:744-754, move a column) — i.e. it fires when the user changes the watchlist column layout while a flash is pending; three occurrences fit the user toggling fields a few times during active ticking (flashes are started on every last-price tick, :948-950). LIFETIME CONTRACT: this is a STALE-CAPTURE lifetime bug (a closure outliving the C++ object it captures), not a missing-parent bug (the timer's parent `self` is correct and intentional) and not a teardown-order bug (teardown is safe: closeEvent calls watchlist_panel.clear() at ui/main_window.py:3568, and `clear` :899-915 stops+clears every timer before setRowCount(0)). The OTHER item-deleting paths are already timer-safe, verified: `remove_symbol` (:841-897) stops the removed row's timers (:874-876) and re-indexes the surviving `_flash_timers` keys (:893-896), and `clear` stops all — I confirmed empirically that removing an earlier/later row and clear() leave no stale timer, so `_rebuild_table` is the SOLE path that deletes flashed items without invalidating the timers. IMPACT: in the shipped app this is LOG SPAM, not breakage — the deleted item's replacement (:686) is created with the default background, so no highlight is stuck or corrupted and the watchlist keeps working; the failed callback would only have reset the already-discarded old item. It can only surface because main.py:3 imports pyqtgraph, whose Qt/__init__.py:314-318 installs a non-abort sys.excepthook (the same mechanism as ESC-032), so the QTimer-slot exception is printed and swallowed (verified: without pyqtgraph a timer-slot exception aborts, rc=134; with pyqtgraph it survives, rc=0). Under PyQt's default hook the process would abort instead.
expected: A flash timer must never touch a QTableWidgetItem that has been deleted. When the flashed cell's item is replaced (a column-layout rebuild) or the row/table is cleared, the pending flash must either be stopped/invalidated or the reset must resolve the item lazily at fire time so it acts on the live cell (or no-ops if the cell is gone).
suggested_direction: Prefer lazy resolution at fire time over capturing the item: replace the :992 closure with a lookup of the current cell at timeout — e.g. a small `_unflash(row, key)` method that does `item = self._item(row, key); if item: item.setBackground(QBrush(QColor('#101218')))`, connected as `timer.timeout.connect(lambda r=row, k=key: self._unflash(r, k))` (mirrors the existing `_set_cell`/:969-974 and `_set_foreground`/:976-979 pattern). This is robust to ANY future item replacement, not just this one. A valid alternative is to invalidate in `_rebuild_table`: stop/clear `_flash_timers` (as `clear` :912-914 already does) before replacing items — semantically fine since the replacement items start default-coloured. What would merely MASK it: wrapping the callback in `try/except RuntimeError`, or `shiboken6.isValid(item)` — both silence the traceback while keeping a dangling intent (and the `isValid` form never resets anything meaningful); avoid them. Regression test (I write none): add a symbol, start a flash (call `_flash(0,'last',GREEN)` or drive `on_tick_price` twice so `old is not None`), then `_on_field_toggled(<inactive field>, True)` (or `panel._apply_columns()`), run the event loop past 400 ms, and assert no unhandled exception fired AND the current cell's background is the default `#101218`. Because pyqtgraph's hook swallows slot exceptions (the test suite imports ui.main_window -> pyqtgraph), the test must NOT rely on the exception propagating to fail it — install a temporary `sys.excepthook` that records unhandled exceptions and assert the record is empty after the wait, and/or assert the observable cell background.

observed: D27.9 aggregator priming (ui/ticker_session.py:1684-1728) hardcodes bar_size='5 secs' (:1711) and builds duration=f'{prime_s} S' with prime_s=min(span_s, _PRIME_MAX_SPAN_S) where _PRIME_MAX_SPAN_S=7200 (:56,1702). IBKR caps the duration for '5 secs' bars at 3600 S (Historical Data Limitations -> Step Sizes; '5 secs' appears only in the 3600 S row; two independent clients document '5 secs up to 3600 S'). For the '4 hours' and '1 day' timeframes span_s exceeds 7200, so the request is exactly duration='7200 S', bar_size='5 secs' -> TWS error 321 'Historical data requested duration is invalid' (verbatim log: 'Aggregator priming request 144 failed [321]'). Reproduced offscreen with now_ts=int(time.time()): 4h/1d -> '7200 S'; 1h -> '1800 S'; all 5-sec requests this loudest on 4h/1d. On failure on_historical_error (:1636-1645) fails open, leaving the aggregator UNPRIMED -> the forming 4h/daily candle's OHLCV is built only from live ticks (AC-D27.9 unmet on those timeframes) and every load emits the warning.
expected: The priming request must be a (durationStr, barSizeSetting) combination IBKR accepts: for bar_size='5 secs' the duration must be <= 3600 S (and >= 60 S). Equivalently, AC-D27.9 ('forming candle reflect primed history') must be met on every timeframe the user can select, including 4h/1d.
suggested_direction: Immediate (within the priming code): clamp the 5-sec priming span to IBKR's 3600 S ceiling, e.g. _PRIME_MAX_SPAN_S hard-capped at 3600 for bar_size='5 secs' (and note the >=60 S floor). But note the deeper mismatch: 5-sec bars cannot cover a 4h (14400 s) or daily (86400 s) forming period at all, so for those timeframes consider priming with a coarser bar size (e.g. '1 min', valid up to '1 D') or seeding from the historical partial bar — that choice is a requirements decision (see the separate REQUIREMENTS finding). Update tests/test_d27_aggregator_priming.py:177 which currently ASSERTS duration == '7200 S' (it enshrines the bug; correct, do not merely weaken).

observed: Owner report: the six SPXW option rows render Type=STOCK (and expiry blank). Root cause proved against the installed ibapi 9.81.1.post1: ui/main_window.py::_on_position_update (:3286-3302) reads contract fields by names ibapi Contract does NOT have. Downstream: _parse_contract_type (ibkr/account.py:42-44, s.strip().lower()) is fine given correct input, but because contract_type is always 'stock', ActivePortfolioPanel._group_and_render (ui/active_portfolio_panel.py:271, filter p.contract_type=='option') never groups option legs, so Strategy/Group never populate for real options.
